subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's worth attention in these goal records.

judge.implied_focus: Goal risk / attention-worthiness (which goals are off-track or overdue and need intervention)

per_column.name: completion_gap
per_column.rationale: Signed gap between target and actual completion; a direct, data-inferable measure of how far a goal is behind, central to identifying at-risk goals.

per_column.name: is_overdue
per_column.rationale: Derived from end_date vs current state; flags goals past deadline, a key facet of attention-worthiness.

per_column.name: attention_flag
per_column.rationale: Explicit classification (On Track / Needs Attention / Cancelled) that operationalises the focus concept directly; the aggregating facet.

per_column.name: duration_days
per_column.rationale: Timeline length between start and end; a contextual attribute that helps interpret gap/overdue status, though somewhat more of a descriptor than a risk driver.

judge.rationale: The columns cohere tightly around one inferable focus: identifying goals that warrant attention because they are behind or overdue. completion_gap (magnitude of shortfall), is_overdue (deadline breach), and attention_flag (a synthesized status) form a coherent multi-facet structure spanning quantitative magnitude, boolean condition, and categorical rollup, rather than a scattered grab-bag or a single restatement. duration_days is a supporting contextual attribute that adds granularity for interpreting the gap. The focus is directly actionable -- an analyst can filter/rank 'Needs Attention' or overdue goals and investigate drivers by department/owner/priority. Minor deduction on structure because attention_flag partly restates the combined signal of the other flags, creating some redundancy, and none of the columns tie the risk to explanatory predictors.
